source.snippet: I have an Automation Event-Triggered Flow that contains a Send Email Message element that sends a Marketing Cloud Next email. In this element, I set From Name and Address using a dropdown. When I retrieve this flow's metadata in my repo, the value of this setting becomes a hardcoded SenderId. This value is org-specific which means that it cannot be used when we deploy to other orgs. My first workaround was to have a Create Record element that gets this senderId and then I assign it to a variable...

problem_statement: Salesforce Marketing Cloud Next flows produce org-specific hardcoded metadata (e.g. SenderId) that breaks CI/CD deployments to other orgs, forcing developers into brittle manual workarounds.
target_segment: Salesforce developers and admins at companies shipping managed packages or maintaining multi-org CI/CD pipelines
notes: Professional dev context — someone building and deploying managed packages commercially. Recurring pain in Salesforce DevOps: org-specific IDs leaking into source-controlled metadata is a well-known class of problem. Single question here but pattern is widespread in the Salesforce ISV/DevOps community. Buyer is a Salesforce developer or ISV team that pays for Salesforce licenses and DevOps tooling.
